claim_1.claim: Hemagglutination Inhibition analysis of serum from 14 subjects sampled one day within a week prior to vaccination (pre-V), at vaccination (day 0), daily days 1 to 10, and day 21 after vaccination showed heterogeneous humoral responses to the three vaccine strains, and by day 21 all subjects except S08 and S12 qualified as immune.

sources.quote: For analysis, peripheral blood was drawn during the week prior to vaccination (pre-V), immediately before vaccination (day 0), daily for days 1–10 and on day 21 post-vaccination. HAI and isotype-specific ELISA assays were performed on serum samples.

No two subjects had identical changes in HAI titers. One subject had no pre-vaccine immunity (HAI < 1 : 40), and five subjects had pre-vaccine immunity (HAI ≥ 1 : 40) to all three viral strains (Fig. 1, Supplementary Table S2). At day 21, all 14 subjects had immunity to A/California, 12 had immunity to A/Perth, and 13 had immunity to B/Brisbane.

claim_2.claim: ELISA analysis of serum from subjects sampled pre-V, day 0, daily days 1 to 10, and day 21 after vaccination showed vaccine-specific IgA, IgG, and IgM levels that paralleled changes in HAI titer, with increases in antibody levels at least 24 hours before S03 and S04.

sources.quote: All three of these subjects had a previous history of influenza vaccination, pre-vaccine immunity to at least one viral vaccine strain by WHO criteria, and strong antibody responses by HAI titer (Fig. 2b, p-values in Supplementary Table S2) and vaccine-specific ELISA (Fig. 2c, p-values in Supplementary Table S2).
(c) Anti-vaccine IgM, IgG, and IgA levels parallel changes in HAI titer (p-values Supplementary Table S2).
S02 had increases in antibody levels at least 24 hours before S03 and S04

claim_3.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of enriched B cells from previously vaccinated subjects S02, S03, and S04 sampled on days 0 to 10 showed appearance of vaccine-specific ASC, migrating CD27hiCD38hiCD20loCD138+ plasma cells, and CD27hiCD38hiCD20loCD138− plasmablasts, with plasmablast and plasma cell populations increasing as ASC appeared; S02 showed peak response at day 5, earlier than S03 and S04.

sources.quote: Cellular responses were seen by FACS in the appearance of vaccine-specific ASC (Fig. 2d), and migrating CD27hiCD38hiCD20loCD138+ plasma cells and CD27hiCD38hiCD20loCD138− plasmablasts (Fig. 2e, p-values in Supplementary Table S4).

(e) Phenotypic changes of CD3−CD19+CD20+CD27− naive B cells, CD19+CD27+CD20+CD38+CD138− memory B cells, CD19+CD27++CD38++CD138− plasmablasts and CD19loCD20loCD27++CD38++CD138+ plasma cells. Plasmablast and plasma cell populations increase as ASC appear (p-values Supplementary Table S4).
S02 showed peak response at day 5, earlier than S03 and S04.

claim_4.claim: ELISpot analysis of B cells from previously vaccinated subjects showed secretion-rate profiles typical of activated ASC, with high-rate vaccine-specific IgG-secreting cells appearing at peak responses and functional vaccine-specific IgA, IgG, and IgM ASC increases as serum antibody levels increased.

sources.quote: In semi-quantitative ELISPOT data, (Supplementary Fig. S2), we found secretion-rate profiles typical of activated ASC15, with high-rate vaccine-specific IgG-secreting cells appearing at peak responses.
(d) ELISPOT assays show functional vaccine-specific IgA, IgG, and IgM ASC increase as serum antibody levels increase.

claim_5.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of B cells from five subjects sampled on days 0 to 10 showed that for three previously vaccinated subjects (S02, S03, and S04), 90% of transcriptome variation could be accounted for by a single eigengenfunction and 742 genes were common to three of five subjects, whereas subjects with predominantly de novo responses (S05, S06) showed two distinct temporal patterns and fewer shared genes.

sources.quote: For three subjects (S02, S03, S04), 90% of transcriptome variation could be accounted for by a single eigenfunction.
Notably, 742 genes were common to three of five subjects.
In two subjects (S05, S06), 90% of the variation in gene expression could be explained by two eigenfunctions, indicating two distinct temporal patterns of gene expression.

claim_6.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of B cells from previously vaccinated subjects S02, S03, and S04 showed transcriptome changes consistent with late B cell differentiation, including increased SDC1/CD138, IRF4, XBP1, CD59, and CXCR3 and decreased MS4A1, CD19, CD5, SERPINB9, PAX5, and BACH2 at peak responses compared to day 0.

sources.quote: Detailed analysis showed known genes with time-varying patterns that paralleled B cell phenotypic changes in S02, S03 and S04 including the genes for CD70 receptor CD2716–18, ecto-enzyme CD3816, plasma cell marker syndecan-1 (SDC1 or CD138), and genes encoding regulatory molecules PRDM1 (Blimp-1)19,7, IRF416,20,21 and XBP122.

Also increased was CD59, which has been associated with memory B cell differentiation23. Increased expression of CXCR3, a gene for a migration marker24 suggested trafficking from the germinal center through peripheral blood presumably to bone marrow and spleen. Decreases in MS4A1 (CD20) and CD19 at peak cellular changes are also consistent with late-stage differentiating B cells16,25,26,23. PAX527 and BACH227 are known repressors of B cell differentiation and decreased gene expression has been linked to expression of PRDM128.
Decreases were seen at peak response in CD5, the gene expressing a marker of naïve B cells, and SERPINB9 (PI-9), an enzyme that protects cytolytic B cells from endogenously produced granzyme B29.

claim_7.claim: Q-PCR analysis of peripheral blood cell isolates from eight subjects collected in two cohorts showed increased expression of CD27, CD38, XBP1, CD59, PRDM1, and IRF4 and decreased expression of IRF8, BACH2, and PAX5 at peak plasmablast/plasma cell expansion, confirming expected B cell differentiation patterns despite heterogeneous vaccine responses.

sources.quote: To confirm and validate changes in expression of key B cell differentiation genes, we probed RNA samples of the eight other subjects by qRT-PCR for 11 genes: SDC1, IGHG, XBP1, CD27, CD38, CD59, PRDM1, IRF4, IRF8, BACH2, and PAX5.
Increased expression of CD27, CD38, XBP1, CD59, PRDM1 and IRF4 and decreased expression of IRF8, BACH2, and PAX5 was expected at peak plasmablast/plasma cell expansion.
While not all genes correlated with phenotype (correlations in Supplementary Table S5), expression levels changed as expected based on phenotype.

claim_8.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of PBMCs collected in parallel with B cell samples from five subjects on days 0 to 10 showed that the primary eigengenfunction peaked on day 1 after vaccination in four of five subjects and was enriched for myeloid/dendritic cell lineage-associated genes, suggesting migration of myeloid/dendritic lineage cells one day post-vaccination.

sources.quote: We found something quite unexpected. The primary eigenfunction in the RNA Seq gene expression data, which explained over 70% of the variation for four out of five subjects (S02, 81.44%; S03, 86.68%; S04, 72.8%; S05, 57.15%; S06, 85.32%), peaked on day 1 post-vaccination (Fig. 7a).

In the predominantly recall subjects, the genes with largest positive loadings on the primary eigenfunction were enriched for myeloid/dendritic cell (DC) lineage-associated genes (Fig. 7b, Supplementary Table S8).
The first eigenfunction for S02, S03, and S04 peaked day 1.
The largest positive loadings on these functions were enriched for genes expressed by myeloid/DC lineages

claim_9.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of in vitro stimulated normal human IgM− B cells from six healthy volunteers showed cells could be FACS-sorted into undivided, CD27lo, and CD27hi differentiation stages for plasma cell differentiation analysis.

sources.quote: Peripheral blood CD27+ IgG+ memory B cells from six normal healthy volunteers were CFSE labeled to track proliferation and stimulated in vitro for 60 hrs with CpG2006 ODN, IL-2, IL-10, IL-15, and BAFF23. For transcriptome analysis, cells were FACS-sorted into three stages of late-stage memory B cell activation and differentiation; undivided CD27lo memory B cell, proliferating CD27lo cells and proliferating CD27hi plasmablasts (Fig. 5b) (n = 6 subjects).
The cells were FACS-sorted into three stages of differentiation (Undivided, CD27lo, and CD27hi).

claim_10.claim: Transcription profiling by array analysis of in vitro differentiated human B cells from six subjects showed that genes upregulated in the plasma cell genes (PCgs) also tended to be upregulated in the most differentiated CD27hi cells, expressed at moderate levels in less differentiated CD27lo cells, and at lowest levels in undivided cells; 366 of 2033 genes differentially expressed between CD27lo and CD27hi cells were shared with the PCgs.

sources.quote: Of 2033 genes differentially expressed between CD27lo and CD27hi B cells, 366 genes of the PCgs were highly expressed in the CD27hi plasmablasts (Fig. 5d, full gene list in Supplementary Table S6).

Genes upregulated in the PCgs also tended to be upregulated in the most differentiated CD27hi cells, expressed at moderate levels in less differentiated CD27lo cells, and at lowest levels in undivided cells. The converse was true of PCgs downregulated genes.
(d) Of 2033 genes significantly differentially expressed between CD27lo and the more differentiated CD27hi plasmablasts, 366 genes were shared with the PCgs
